why_possibly_novel: Per-pixel cross-task closure as an adaptive weighting signal, evaluated jointly on all three outputs in adverse strata, appears unexplored beyond fixed multi-task formulations (unverified).
minimal_falsification_experiment: Extend a joint depth-flow-pose framework with closure-residual-driven weighting, train on mixed-condition data, and evaluate all three outputs on adverse-condition GT benchmarks against fixed-weight and independent baselines.
main_risk: Closure residuals conflate estimator error with genuine dynamic content, requiring the dynamic-region pathway to be handled separately or the mechanism degrades scenes with motion.
community_default_belief: The self-supervised geometry triad is a mature, saturated recipe with only incremental gains left.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Saturation was measured on clear-weather benchmarks; the fixed-weight formulation was never stress-tested where its independence assumptions break, which is exactly where headroom should be largest.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Two GPU-days: closure-weighted fine-tuning versus fixed weights on one adverse-condition benchmark, joint metric deltas.
kill_threshold: Kill if adaptive weighting improves adverse-condition depth AbsRel and trajectory error by under 10% relative each over fixed weighting.

one_line_idea: Novel-view-synthesis metric families disagree enough to flip method rankings at publication-relevant margins, and a metric-agreement audit across the published method spectrum will quantify how much NVS progress is metric-choice artifact.
problem: NVS papers claim superiority on margins of fractions of a decibel or small perceptual-metric deltas, choosing among several standard metrics whose disagreement structure has never been quantified across the method population.
core_hypothesis: The three standard metric families weight blur, hallucinated detail, and color fidelity differently enough that method rankings are unstable within typical claimed margins; a fraction of published pairwise superiority claims would reverse under a different standard metric, making metric choice a hidden researcher degree of freedom.
falsifiable_prediction: Re-evaluating a broad slate of public NVS methods under all standard metrics on identical scenes will show pairwise rank flips in a meaningful fraction of method pairs whose claimed margins are within typical publication deltas, with flips concentrated between methods differing in hallucination propensity.
why_important: If typical margins are within metric-disagreement noise, the field needs multi-metric or geometry-grounded reporting standards before further leaderboard optimization is meaningful.
why_possibly_novel: Population-level metric-agreement quantification across NVS methods, with flip-rate versus claimed-margin analysis, appears unpublished (unverified).
minimal_falsification_experiment: Reproduce a slate of public methods on standard scene sets, compute all metric families under one protocol, and report the flip-rate matrix and its relationship to margin size and method type.
main_risk: Reproduction fidelity and protocol details (crop, tone mapping) affect metrics; the protocol must be locked and published first.
community_default_belief: The standard NVS metrics agree well enough that any of them certifies method superiority at published margins.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Each metric family encodes different perceptual assumptions, and modern methods differ exactly on the axes (hallucination versus blur) where the families disagree most.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One GPU-day: six public methods on one scene set, cross-metric flip-rate table.
kill_threshold: Kill if under 10% of pairwise comparisons with margins below typical publication deltas flip across metric families.

family_fingerprint.manipulated_variable: metric family on fixed method outputs

one_line_idea: Depth benchmark test scenes leak into web-scale pretraining corpora, and a retrieval-based contamination audit will quantify how much reported zero-shot depth generalization is memorization of the evaluation scenes themselves.
problem: Depth foundation models pretrain on massive weakly documented image corpora and then report zero-shot numbers on benchmarks whose imagery has circulated online for a decade, without contamination analysis.
core_hypothesis: Standard depth test sets are partially present (exactly or as near-duplicates from the same physical spaces) in web-scale corpora; models will perform measurably better on contaminated test items than on matched-difficulty uncontaminated items, inflating generalization claims.
falsifiable_prediction: Near-duplicate retrieval between test sets and accessible pretraining corpora will find nontrivial contamination rates, and per-item analysis will show contaminated items scoring systematically better than matched uncontaminated items for models trained on those corpora but not for models with clean training sets.
why_important: Zero-shot depth claims steer deployment trust; a quantified contamination discount, and a certified-clean evaluation subset as the constructive output, would put the field's headline numbers on honest footing.
why_possibly_novel: Contamination auditing is established for language and classification; a systematic depth-benchmark audit with performance-delta attribution appears missing (unverified).
minimal_falsification_experiment: Run scalable near-duplicate and same-scene retrieval between benchmark test imagery and open pretraining corpora, stratify test items by contamination status, and compare model error across strata with difficulty matching.
main_risk: Closed corpora cannot be audited directly, limiting attribution for proprietary models; open-corpus models give the causal anchor.
community_default_belief: Zero-shot depth benchmark performance reflects genuine cross-domain generalization to unseen scenes.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Benchmark imagery is among the most-downloaded, most-reposted visual content in the field, making it disproportionately likely to appear in any web crawl.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One GPU-day: retrieval audit of one benchmark against one open corpus, contamination rate estimate.
kill_threshold: Kill if contamination is under 1% of test items and contaminated-item error advantage is under 5% relative, showing the concern is negligible.

one_line_idea: Chamfer distance is blind to topological errors that decide downstream success: a topology-aware reconstruction metric validated against robot navigation and interaction outcomes will re-rank reconstruction methods by fitness for use.
problem: Surface reconstruction is ranked by point-distance metrics that barely penalize topology mistakes (merged walls and openings, disconnected parts, phantom handles), while downstream consumers fail on exactly those mistakes.
core_hypothesis: A metric family combining distance with topological agreement (connectivity, holes, passage structure relative to GT) will predict downstream task success (simulated navigation, grasp planning) far better than chamfer and F-score, and will materially re-rank published reconstruction methods.
falsifiable_prediction: Across reconstruction outputs spanning methods and quality levels, the topology-aware metric will correlate with simulated navigation and interaction success substantially better than distance metrics, and method rankings under it will differ from chamfer rankings on a meaningful fraction of pairs.
why_important: Metrics are the objective function of the research community; a use-validated metric redirects reconstruction research toward failures that actually matter and gives practitioners a fitness-for-purpose selector.
why_possibly_novel: Topology-sensitive geometry metrics exist in isolation; validation against embodied task outcomes as the ground truth for metric quality appears missing (unverified).
minimal_falsification_experiment: Generate reconstructions of simulation-ready scenes across methods, run navigation and interaction tasks in simulation on each reconstruction, and compare how well candidate metrics predict task success.
main_risk: Simulated task success may itself be an unrepresentative proxy for real robot outcomes, requiring a small real-robot confirmation subset.
community_default_belief: Chamfer distance and F-score adequately capture reconstruction quality for practical purposes.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Point-distance metrics integrate error uniformly over surfaces, while task failure is caused by sparse, structurally decisive errors; the metric and the consumer literally measure different things.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Two GPU-days: 20 reconstructions, simulated navigation success versus chamfer and versus the topology metric, correlation comparison.
kill_threshold: Kill if the topology-aware metric fails to beat chamfer's task-success correlation by at least 0.15 absolute correlation, or if rankings agree over 90%.

one_line_idea: Point-tracking benchmark averages hide that leading models are still poor on thin structures and self-similar textures: difficulty-stratified re-annotation of existing benchmarks will reveal large headroom the leaderboard says does not exist.
problem: Point-tracking leaderboards are approaching saturation on standard benchmarks, generating a solved-problem narrative, but per-point difficulty attributes (structure width, texture self-similarity, motion complexity) are not annotated, so error concentration is invisible.
core_hypothesis: Aggregate scores are dominated by easy points (large textured surfaces); annotating existing benchmarks with per-point difficulty attributes will reveal strata (thin structures, repeated patterns, fast rotation) where accuracy remains far below the average, with consistent cross-model failure patterns indicating shared architectural blind spots.
falsifiable_prediction: Stratified re-scoring of public trackers will show the hardest annotated strata scoring dramatically below the benchmark average, model rankings differing per stratum, and progress-over-time curves that are nearly flat on the hard strata despite steep aggregate improvement.
why_important: Where benchmarks saturate, research funding and attention move on; if the saturation is compositional illusion, the field abandons an unsolved problem, and the stratified benchmark revives it at near-zero collection cost.
why_possibly_novel: Difficulty-attribute re-annotation of existing tracking benchmarks with progress-curve re-analysis appears not to have been done (unverified).
minimal_falsification_experiment: Define objective difficulty attributes computable from GT and imagery, annotate existing benchmark points, re-score public trackers per stratum, and reconstruct historical progress curves per stratum from released checkpoints.
main_risk: Attribute definitions could be gerrymandered toward the conclusion; preregistering attribute definitions before scoring guards against this.
community_default_belief: Near-saturated averages mean point tracking is effectively solved on the benchmark domain.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Averages weight strata by frequency, not by importance; benchmark point sampling favored trackable points at annotation time, baking easiness into the aggregate.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One GPU-day: annotate thin-structure and self-similarity attributes on one benchmark subset, stratified re-score of two trackers.
kill_threshold: Kill if hard-stratum accuracy is within 10% relative of the benchmark average, showing no hidden headroom.

one_line_idea: The claimed closure of the synthetic-to-real gap in optical flow does not survive rolling-shutter and exposure realities: real-camera-artifact-stratified evaluation will reopen the gap that clean benchmark transfers declared closed.
problem: Recent results show synthetic-trained flow transferring well to standard real benchmarks, and the community increasingly treats the domain gap as closed, but the real benchmarks were captured with atypically clean acquisition (global shutter, controlled exposure).
core_hypothesis: Consumer video differs from both synthetic data and clean benchmarks through acquisition artifacts (rolling shutter skew, auto-exposure fluctuation, compression); flow accuracy on artifact-rich real footage degrades substantially, so the gap was redefined, not closed, and artifact simulation in training will recover much of the loss.
falsifiable_prediction: Constructing evaluation sets with GT proxies on artifact-rich captures (dual-camera rigs pairing clean and consumer cameras) will show synthetic-trained models losing accuracy relative to clean-capture evaluation by margins far exceeding the residual clean-benchmark gap, with artifact-augmented retraining recovering a large fraction.
why_important: The synthetic-data strategy for flow rests on the gap-closure claim; if closure is an artifact of clean evaluation hardware, training pipelines need artifact modeling, and benchmark builders need consumer-camera tracks.
why_possibly_novel: Acquisition-artifact stratification as the missing axis in flow domain-gap analysis, with paired-camera GT transfer, appears unexamined (unverified).
minimal_falsification_experiment: Build a paired-rig dataset (clean camera plus consumer camera, GT flow transferred via calibration), evaluate public models per condition, and run artifact-augmentation retraining as the intervention arm.
main_risk: GT transfer between paired cameras has its own error floor, which must be quantified below the effect size being measured.
community_default_belief: The synthetic-to-real gap in optical flow is essentially closed by modern training data and architectures.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Both sides of the closure evidence share the clean-acquisition property; the conclusion generalizes over a variable that was never varied.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One capture session plus one GPU-day: paired-camera clips, per-condition accuracy delta for one model.
kill_threshold: Kill if artifact-rich accuracy loss is under 1.5x the residual clean-benchmark gap, confirming closure holds broadly.

one_line_idea: A meaningful share of recent indoor-reconstruction leaderboard movement is attributable to mesh post-processing choices rather than model improvements, and a standardized-backend re-evaluation will separate the two contributions method by method.
problem: Indoor reconstruction methods differ simultaneously in learned components and in post-processing (fusion parameters, meshing algorithms, cleanup heuristics), and papers report only the composite result.
core_hypothesis: Post-processing choices move geometry metrics by amounts comparable to claimed method deltas; re-running published methods' learned outputs through one standardized fusion-and-meshing backend will compress the leaderboard and reassign a measurable share of claimed progress to the post-processing axis, with a mechanism-level account of which backend choices matter.
falsifiable_prediction: Under a standardized backend, the spread between recent methods will shrink substantially, some published orderings will invert, and a decomposition will attribute a nontrivial fraction of aggregate leaderboard movement to backend differences, with fusion truncation and hole-filling settings as dominant factors.
why_important: Correct attribution determines what the field builds next; if backends drive results, backend science deserves first-class attention and papers need factored reporting requirements.
why_possibly_novel: Standardized-backend re-evaluation with variance decomposition across a method population appears missing for reconstruction benchmarks (unverified).
minimal_falsification_experiment: Collect public checkpoints of recent methods, extract their pre-fusion predictions, run all through one backend grid, and decompose metric variance into model versus backend components.
main_risk: Some methods entangle learned components with their backend, making clean extraction impossible and requiring those methods to be analyzed separately.
community_default_belief: Reconstruction leaderboard gains reflect improvements in the learned reconstruction models themselves.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Post-processing is unregulated, high-leverage, and tuned per paper on the same test scenes, which is precisely the recipe for absorbing untracked gains.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One GPU-day: three methods through two backends, spread-compression measurement.
kill_threshold: Kill if backend standardization changes method spread by under 15% relative and inverts no published orderings.

one_line_idea: Label-free evaluation of video and 3D perception via internal geometric consistency (reconstruction closure across views and time) correlates strongly with supervised rankings, enabling benchmark-free model selection on any target domain.
problem: Perception models can only be ranked where labeled benchmarks exist, but deployment domains rarely match benchmark domains, forcing blind model selection precisely where it matters.
core_hypothesis: For geometric tasks, correctness has an internal signature: outputs of a good model are mutually consistent under reprojection, temporal transport, and loop closure on unlabeled target footage; a consistency score computed from these closures will rank models nearly as well as ground-truth benchmarks do, because large violations of internal consistency cannot coexist with accuracy.
falsifiable_prediction: Across model families for depth, flow, and reconstruction, the unlabeled consistency score computed on benchmark imagery (ignoring labels) will correlate strongly with labeled rankings, and its per-domain scores will predict which model wins after domain-specific fine-tuning evaluation, subject to a measurable failure mode for degenerate constant outputs that the score must be shown to penalize.
why_important: A validated label-free ranking protocol turns every deployment domain into its own benchmark, changing how practitioners select and monitor geometric perception systems at scale.
why_possibly_novel: Consistency-based unsupervised metrics exist for single tasks; a validated cross-task protocol with degenerate-solution safeguards and correlation-to-supervised-rankings evidence appears missing (unverified).
minimal_falsification_experiment: Implement the closure score suite, compute it for public model slates on labeled benchmarks, report rank correlation against supervised metrics per task, and stress-test against degenerate and adversarially smooth outputs.
main_risk: Models could achieve consistency through shared bias (all views wrong the same way); cross-model disagreement terms and physical constraints must catch this class.
community_default_belief: Trustworthy model ranking requires labeled ground truth; unsupervised proxies are too gameable to rely on.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Geometry is over-constrained: faking consistency across many independent closures is nearly as hard as being correct, a structural property that label-free evaluation in non-geometric domains lacks.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One GPU-day: consistency score versus labeled ranking for five depth models on one benchmark, rank correlation.
kill_threshold: Kill if rank correlation with supervised orderings is below 0.7 on any of the three tasks, or if degenerate outputs evade the safeguards.

family_fingerprint.manipulated_variable: internal consistency score as ranking criterion
